source.title: Depth Without the Magic: Inductive Bias of Natural Gradient Descent
source.authors: A. Kerekes; Anna M'esz'aros; Ferenc Huszár

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own generalization experiments showing that exact natural gradient can fail where Euclidean gradient descent with a suitable parameterization succeeds, qualifying broad claims about optimization and parameterization. The tasks are synthetic and do not directly test the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies exact natural gradient flow/descent and Euclidean gradient descent in synthetic sparse classification and matrix completion. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows. Figure-only plot values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests parameterization-dependent generalization under exact natural gradient and Euclidean gradient methods in synthetic linear classification and matrix completion. None of its results tests V1–V8. In particular, NGD versus full-batch EGD does not test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison under limited tuning on image or language benchmarks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. In the studied deep linear problems, exact natural gradient loses useful parameterization-dependent inductive biases and can generalize worse than suitably parameterized Euclidean gradient descent. The authors explicitly allow that natural gradient may generalize better in other settings.
record.recipe_differences: Exact natural gradient flow/descent and full-batch Euclidean gradient descent in synthetic deep linear classification and matrix-factorization tasks; not the original studies' methods or benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Fisher estimate changes the sparse-classification outcome: population Fisher improves NGD relative to training-sample Fisher, but remains below EGD. Parameterization depth changes EGD results. In matrix completion, deep factorization EGD generalizes while NGD does not.

fits_no_version.finding: In 1000-dimensional sparse classification, sample-Fisher NGD performs at chance for N < D and worse than EGD for N ≥ D. Population Fisher improves NGD but remains below EGD. Two- and three-layer diagonal EGD perform best, jointly reaching about 90%; four-layer EGD is comparable to shallow EGD after the tested training duration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact natural gradient can generalize worse than Euclidean gradient with a suitable parameterization in synthetic sparse classification; Fisher estimation and parameterization depth affect the comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: In rank-5 matrix completion, deep matrix-product EGD recovers low-rank structure, whereas NGD behaves like direct-parameterization EGD and fails to predict unobserved entries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Natural-gradient parameterization invariance can eliminate the useful implicit regularization of deep matrix-factorization EGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing initialization through collapsed deeper matrix products has negligible effects on test loss compared with changing training dynamics in the tested matrix-factorization models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training dynamics account for more of the observed generalization differences than the tested initialization-depth changes in deep linear matrix factorization.

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic sparse classification and matrix completion rather than natural image or language datasets. Exact numerical outcomes are largely presented in figures, with qualitative descriptions in the text. The paper analyzes full-batch gradient flow/descent and notes that stochastic-gradient behavior is not addressed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numerical or explicit results identified beyond the extracted qualitative experiment findings; cited prior work excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on image and language benchmarks, including tuning, weight decay, and switching conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that reduce those effects.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a correlate and ranking measure of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because no row measures a listed version; this does not dispute the reported experimental outcomes. Citations to Wilson et al. and Jiang et al. supply context rather than new tests of V4 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No Adam, SGD or momentum-SGD comparison.

rows.subject: NGD
rows.operation_detail: Natural gradient descent with Fisher averaged on training samples in a sparse classification task.
rows.note: The text describes performance qualitatively; precise plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The chance-level result is correctly reported, but measures none of V1–V8; its original absent state cannot be interpreted as a verdict on those versions.

rows.subject: NGD (pop.)
rows.operation_detail: Natural gradient descent with Fisher averaged over a much larger sample set (population Fisher).
rows.value: generalization performance improved, but still did not match EGD
rows.note: Qualitative outcome stated in text; no exact plotted accuracy supplied.
rows.check: Population Fisher improves NGD without matching EGD, but this is not a test of any listed version. The text's overall comparison is not confined to N < D.

rows.subject: EGD, L = 1
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent in direct parameterization on a synthetic sparse classification task.
rows.baseline: NGD, which performs at chance level when N < D
rows.value: less successful than EGD in diagonal parametrizations; exact value not stated
rows.note: Text compares the methods but does not state the direct model's exact accuracy for this condition.
rows.check: Direct-parameterization EGD is a valid experimental comparator, but its relative accuracy measures none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: EGD, L = 2
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent in a two-layer diagonal parameterization on a synthetic sparse classification task.
rows.baseline: NGD, which performs at chance level when N < D
rows.note: The text groups L = 2 and L = 3 as reaching up to 90%; it does not assign that maximum separately to each.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. The maximum accuracy of about 90% is reported jointly for L = 2 and L = 3; it should not be assigned independently to each depth.

rows.subject: EGD, L = 3
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent in a three-layer diagonal parameterization on a synthetic sparse classification task.
rows.baseline: NGD, which performs at chance level when N < D
rows.note: The text groups L = 2 and L = 3 as reaching up to 90%; it does not assign that maximum separately to each.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. The maximum accuracy of about 90% is reported jointly for L = 2 and L = 3; it should not be assigned independently to each depth.

rows.subject: EGD, L = 4
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent in a four-layer diagonal parameterization on a synthetic sparse classification task.
rows.value: on par with the shallow solution
rows.note: Authors suggest two million EGD steps may not have been enough for implicit regularization to take effect.
rows.check: The reported parity with shallow EGD concerns depth and finite training duration, not V2's width sweep. Insufficient training is the authors' explanation, not an established result.

rows.subject: NGD
rows.operation_detail: Natural gradient descent with training-sample Fisher on a synthetic sparse classification task.
rows.value: performs worse than EGD even when N ≥ D
rows.note: Qualitative outcome stated; no exact accuracy values supplied.
rows.check: Worse accuracy for NGD than EGD is correctly described, but reverses none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: NGD
rows.operation_detail: Natural gradient descent in deep matrix factorization for matrix completion.
rows.measure: Test loss / generalization to unobserved entries
rows.note: The text states the qualitative result; precise test-loss values are shown only in plots.
rows.check: Matrix-completion generalization measures none of V1–V8. The 1000-dimensional size belongs to the classification experiment and is unsupported here. The authors mean complete failure to predict unobserved entries, rather than merely incomplete generalization.

rows.subject: EGD, L ≥ 2
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent in deep matrix-product parameterizations for matrix completion.
rows.value: can reach low training error and identify low-rank solutions
rows.note: The text describes qualitative performance; no precise plotted values are reconstructed.
rows.check: Low-rank recovery under deep matrix factorization measures none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: EGD, L = 2 and L = 3
rows.operation_detail: Euclidean gradient descent after initializing from collapsed deeper matrix-factorization models to isolate initialization effects.
rows.value: initialization plays a negligible role in the inductive bias of EGD in deep matrix factorization
rows.note: The figure varies initialization depth; text characterizes its effect as negligible.
rows.check: The initialization comparison in Figure 5 right measures test loss, not effective rank at convergence. Its correct text locator is Section 5.2's initialization discussion, not Section 3.1 Experiment 2. The conclusion concerns initialization's comparatively negligible effect on generalization in these experiments.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
